caption: The drawing features a vertically oriented rectangular composition divided into three main sections. The upper section displays a repeating diamond-shaped pattern, within which are symmetric floral or star motifs, all rendered in shades of tan, brown, and muted yellow. Below this patterned section is a thin horizontal brown strip that separates it from the middle section. The middle section consists of a geometric grid arrangement of three-dimensional square forms, each square shaded in tones of beige, yellow, and brown to give a faceted, raised appearance. A second, slightly darker brown horizontal band separates this grid from the bottom section. The bottom section is an area filled with a diffuse, marbled wash of pale yellow, tan, and brown hues without any defined pattern. The entire panel sits centrally on an off-white background, and the lower right corner bears the small, printed text “FANNY S. PARASKE.”
title: Wall Decoration, on Adobe Ranch House
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
